question: Three rods AB, BC and BD made of the same material and having the same area of cross-section and the same length are joined at B, as in a T-shape. The ends A, C and D are held at temperatures $20°$C, $80°$C and $80°$C respectively. The temperature at the junction B of the three rods is
solution:
In the steady state the net heat flowing into B is zero. The rods are identical, so each current is proportional to its temperature difference:
$$(80 - \theta) + (80 - \theta) = \theta - 20 \;\Rightarrow\; 3\theta = 180 \;\Rightarrow\; \theta = 60°\text{C}$$
